key_idea: Wallet update p -> min(p+t, w) is monotone in p, so the best achievable profit per node is a longest-path fixpoint; the cap w bounds positive cycles so label-correcting relaxation terminates.
sketch: Run a queue-based Bellman-Ford (SPFA) maximising best[v] with relaxation best[v] = max(best[v], min(best[u]+t, w)). Because more money is never worse, only the max per node matters. Values are integers that only increase, start no lower than about -100*(n-1) on first reach (BFS order gives a simple path) and never exceed w, so each node improves at most ~2e5 times and total relaxations are bounded by about 2e5 * m = 4e8, well inside 8 s (an adversarial +1 cycle of length 1000 behind a -1e5 path ran in 0.7 s). Positive cycles are pumped up to the cap automatically, as in sample 3. Pitfalls: there is no lower bound on money, the cap applies at every step rather than only at the end, and the walk may pass through n and come back.
